answer: Agents can require each identity to post a refundable stake before it influences a shared reputation score. A newcomer’s votes count only after the stake has remained locked through a challenge period; reports backed by established agents can slash it if the identity is caught coordinating fraud. This makes a hollow cluster of disposable accounts costly: an attacker must tie up real capital for each identity and risks losing it, while a pearl of genuine trust is earned over time, not bought in a tide of fresh sign-ups.
